competitors.title: Claude Code Agent Teams: How Multi-Agent AI Development Works in 2026
key_points: Agent Teams shipped Feb 5, 2026 alongside Claude Opus 4.6 — experimental, behind CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 env var
Architecture: Team Lead + Teammates + Mailbox system (peer-to-peer communication) + Shared Task List
Subagents follow strict parent-child hierarchy; Agent Teams use peer-to-peer mailbox system for true collaboration
3-agent team uses ~2.5-4x tokens of single agent but completes in 1/2 to 1/3 the wall-clock time
Claude Code Review (March 9, 2026) increased Anthropic internal code review coverage from 16% to 54% using multi-agent PR analysis
Team patterns: Full-stack squads, Migration squads, Security review teams, Microservices coordinators, Test blitz, Documentation squads
Limitations: file conflict resolution, mailbox latency, experimental stability, no persistent teams, debugging complexity
Requirements: Opus 4.6+, Pro ($20/mo), Max ($100-200/mo), Team ($150/user/mo), or Enterprise plan

competitors.title: Claude Code Multi-Agent Coordination: Build AI Teams That Ship (2026)
key_points: Five distinct coordination patterns: Sync subagents (blocking), Async agents (background), Fork subagents (cache-optimized), Teammates (named inter-agent messaging), Remote agents (separate CCR environments)
Git worktree isolation: each agent gets its own working directory sharing .git history - prevents file conflicts during parallel editing
Fork subagents inherit parent's system prompt for cache-identical API prefixes, reducing latency and cost
Agent Teams use named agent registry with SendMessage tool for fully connected communication graph
MCP server requirement declarations: agents declare required servers before execution, system polls up to 30s for availability
Optimal team size: 2-4 parallel agents hit sweet spot between speedup and coordination overhead
Scout-Implement-Verify pattern: sync scout -> async parallel implementation -> sync verification
Continuous Reviewer pattern: dedicated reviewer agent provides near-real-time feedback as implementers commit
Wall-clock example: 3-min implement + 2-min test + 1-min doc = 3min parallel instead of 6min sequential

competitors.title: Claude Code Agent Teams, Subagents, and MCP: The 2026 Playbook
key_points: Claude Code's moat is the orchestration surface: project memory, tool access, MCP, subagents, hooks, skills
Best subagents are boring and specific: code-reviewer, test-runner, frontend-qa, docs-maintainer, security-checker, migration-planner
MCP turns agents from coding assistants into operators connecting to issue trackers, databases, monitoring, browser automation
Hooks control workflow with TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted events - enforces project rules
Opus 4.6 brings 1M token context window in beta, longer agentic tasks, larger codebase handling
Production pattern: one main agent owns plan/integration, specialist subagents handle bounded tasks with own context and tool budget
Winning combination: strong planner model, clear subagent boundaries, tool-specific permissions, test feedback, human review at checkpoints

competitors.title: Orchestrate Teams of Claude Code Sessions - Official Claude Code Docs
key_points: Agent teams vs subagents: subagents report results back to main agent only; teammates message each other directly with shared task list
Teammates have own context window, fully independent, with task self-coordination
Token cost: subagents lower (results summarized); agent teams higher (each teammate is separate Claude instance)
Enable via CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 in settings.json or env var
Two display modes: in-process (Shift+Down cycle) and split panes (requires tmux or iTerm2)
Subagent definitions can be reused as teammate roles, with tools allowlist and model selection
Teammates share permissions with lead, each runs full Claude instance with CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, skills
Team config stored at ~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/config.json, ephemeral (removed on cleanup)
Best practices: 3-5 teammates, 5-6 tasks per teammate, start with research/review tasks, avoid file conflicts

competitors.title: Claude Code Multiple Agent Systems: Complete 2026 Guide
key_points: Three approaches: official subagents (production-ready, stable), experimental Swarms (feature-flagged, undocumented), third-party frameworks
Swarms mode discovered Jan 24, 2026 via claude-sneakpeek tool - team lead plans/delegates, specialist background agents execute
Third-party frameworks: Claude Flow (12.9k stars, 60+ agents, 84.8% SWE-Bench), oh-my-claudecode (2.6k stars, 5 modes), Claude Squad (5.8k stars, multi-tool), ccswarm (Rust-native)
Gartner: multi-agent inquiries surged 1,445% Q1 2024-Q2 2025; 40% of enterprise apps will have task-specific AI agents by end of 2026
Subagents defined in Markdown with YAML frontmatter: name, description, model, color, tools allowlist
Common personas: System Architect, Code Reviewer, Debugger, DevOps Engineer, Test specialists (Playwright suite)
Best practice: max 3-4 subagents per workflow, include weaknesses in system prompt, make agents critical not agreeable

competitors.title: Code with Claude 2026: Dreams, Routines & Multi-Agent Orchestration
key_points: Code with Claude 2026 conference (May 6, 2026): Agent Dreaming (self-improving agents), Routines (scheduled automation), Outcome-based evaluation, multi-agent orchestration, doubled session limits
Agent Dreaming: agents review past sessions, identify patterns, refine memory/behavior without human intervention
Claude Code Routines: scheduled/webhook-triggered automation (e.g., daily PR reviews at 9AM, weekly dependency scans)
Outcome-based agents use rubric grading evaluating actual results vs process compliance
Anthropic doubling down on agent infrastructure (memory, scheduling, evaluation, orchestration) vs raw model capability
